overrides.//: Core may not reach into a feature. Core is what features are built ON; a core file that knows a feature's name has inverted the dependency, and the first symptom is that deleting the feature breaks the bootstrap. The one legal exception is src/features/index.js and src/features/config.js, which are the loaders and live under features/ precisely so this rule can name them.

patterns.message: Core must not import from inside a feature. Go through the loader (src/features), or promote the thing you want to src/core - once there is a second consumer for it.

overrides.//: A feature may not reach into another feature. If two need the same thing, it is promoted to core. util/pager came out of sigma exactly this way, when a second consumer appeared for it. The pattern matches any sibling; the feature's own files are relative paths that never contain 'features/', so they are unaffected.

patterns.message: A feature must not import another feature. Promote the shared thing to src/core - but only once there is a genuine second consumer, not in anticipation of one.

overrides.//: The config load path. config/index.js builds its export at require time, so anything reachable from a feature's config.js during that build must not require config/ back. The cycle does not throw - it silently hands out a half-built object, and because tests/setup.js depends on that export the symptom lands somewhere unrelated. The `s` accessor is passed in as an argument for this reason.

patterns.message: A feature's config.js must not require config/ - that is a load-order cycle. Use the `s` accessor you were passed; it IS the config accessor.
A feature's config.js must not require core either: most of core requires config, so this is the same cycle one hop further out. Node builtins are fine.
